equation_request.abstract: Adiabatic quantum computing (AQC) is based on the adiabatic principle, where a quantum system remains in an instantaneous eigenstate of the driving Hamiltonian. The final state of the Hamiltonian encodes solution to the problem of interest. While AQC has distinct advantages, recent researches have shown that quantumness such as quantum coherence in adiabatic processes may be lost entirely due to the system-bath interaction when the evolution time is long, and consequently the expected quantum speedup dose not show up. Here we propose a fast-signal assisted adiabatic quantum algorithm. We find that by applying a sequence of fast random or regular signals during the evolution process, the runtime can be reduced greatly, yet advantages of the adiabatic algorithm remain intact. Significantly, we present a randomized Trotter formula and show that the driving Hamiltonian and the sequence of fast signals can be implemented simultaneously. We apply the algorithm for solving the $3$-bit exact cover problem (EC$3$) and put forward an approach for implementing the problem with trapped ions.

specification.problem: Adiabatic quantum computing with an added sequence of fast (random or regular) signals to shorten runtime, applied to a tiny instance of the 3-bit exact cover (EC3) problem. Only the generic adiabatic interpolation and a generic randomized product-formula picture can be reconstructed from the abstract.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: standard AQC interpolation H(s)=(1-s)H_B+sH_P on n=3 qubits, with an assumed fast-signal term and an assumed generic randomized Trotter step. Out of scope: the paper's specific signal sequences, the actual randomized Trotter formula and its error analysis, the open-system/decoherence modeling, the specific EC3 clause instance, and the trapped-ion implementation.

symbols.meaning: number of qubits (bits of the EC3 instance)
symbols.domain: positive integer; n=3 in the assumed tiny instance

symbols.meaning: problem Hamiltonian whose ground state encodes the solution
random signal sign/amplitude in step k (assumed)

equations.label: Adiabatic interpolation
equations.description: Standard AQC driving Hamiltonian; the final ground state encodes the solution.
equations.justification: Standard AQC form consistent with the abstract's description of a driving Hamiltonian whose final state encodes the solution; the paper's schedule is not given.

equations.label: Fast-signal-assisted Hamiltonian
equations.description: Driving Hamiltonian plus a rapidly varying random or regular signal term.
equations.justification: The abstract only says fast random or regular signals are applied during evolution; the operator form is a placeholder.
assumptions: Signal operators σ_j and time dependence ξ_j(t) are unspecified in the abstract

equations.label: Randomized product step
equations.description: Generic randomized Trotter-like discretization in which driving and signal are applied together in each step.
equations.justification: The abstract says a randomized Trotter formula allows simultaneous implementation; the actual formula is not stated, so this is a generic stand-in. It is an approximation, not exact equality.
assumptions: Each step exponentiates the combined Hamiltonian, or its split terms
Sampling distribution of ξ_k and j_k unspecified

equations.label: Adiabatic condition (background)
equations.description: Standard sufficient condition for adiabatic following, setting the long runtime that the fast signals aim to reduce.
equations.justification: Well-known textbook condition, not taken from the abstract.
assumptions: Nondegenerate ground state along the path

equations.label: EC3 problem Hamiltonian (generic form)
equations.description: Generic exact cover 3 penalty Hamiltonian: each clause is satisfied iff exactly one of its three bits equals 1; zero energy means a solution.
equations.justification: Common EC3 encoding in the AQC literature; the paper's instance and form may differ.
assumptions: Clause set C is not given in the abstract and must be chosen

registers.name: q
registers.role: Qubits encoding the EC3 bits, computational basis bit string z_1z_2z_3 with q_1 as most significant

specification.initial_state: Assumed ground state of H_B, e.g. H_B=-\sum_i\sigma^x_i gives the uniform superposition |+\rangle^{\otimes n}.

steps.description: Choose a tiny EC3 instance (clause set C) and build H_P and a driver H_B.
Prepare the ground state of H_B.
Evolve under H(s) plus the assumed fast-signal term over total time T, with T shorter than the adiabatic-condition estimate.
Discretize with a randomized Trotter-like product so driving and signals act in the same step.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of all qubits at the end; a low-energy outcome under H_P indicates an EC3 solution.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Check the measured bit string against the EC3 clauses and repeat on failure.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was given, so a 3-qubit EC3 instance with generic AQC was chosen as the smallest construction
Signal form, schedule and randomized Trotter formula are placeholders, not the paper's
missing_information: Exact form and statistics of the fast signals
The paper's randomized Trotter formula and its error bounds
The specific EC3 instance and driver Hamiltonian
Quantitative runtime reduction and decoherence model
